findings.issue_text: Posts imported via RSS/remote retrieval use `cook_method: raw_html` bypassing sanitization, and are rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, allowing stored XSS from malicious external feeds.
`open(url).read` in `import_remote` uses `Kernel#open` with user-supplied URL, enabling SSRF and local file reads via non-HTTP schemes and redirects.
Origin validation `discourseUrl.indexOf(e.origin) === -1` is a substring check rather than exact match, allowing malicious origins to bypass validation.
The `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML string without escaping in `topic_embed.rb:15`, causing stored XSS via URLs containing single quotes or angle brackets.
`open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `poll_feed.rb:31` uses `Kernel#open` with an admin-configurable URL, risking local file exposure via `file://` schemes if settings are compromised.
`i.content.scrub` in `poll_feed.rb:33` will raise `NoMethodError` if the RSS item lacks a `content` element.
`Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs synchronously inside the `RetrieveTopic` job worker, blocking it; should be enqueued asynchronously via `Jobs.enqueue`.
When no topic exists, a `RetrieveTopic` job is enqueued on every request, potentially flooding the job queue before Redis throttling takes effect.
Referer-based host validation in `embed_controller.rb:26` can be bypassed using spoofed or empty referer headers.
`absolutize_urls` in `topic_embed.rb:58` checks port numbers regardless of scheme, causing incorrect absolute URL prefixes for `https://` on port 80 or `http://` on port 443.

goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Posts imported via RSS/remote retrieval use `cook_method: raw_html` bypassing sanitization, and are rendered with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, allowing stored XSS from malicious external feeds.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces a `raw_html` cook method that makes `Post#cook` return `raw` directly (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`), skipping the normal cooking/rendering pipeline where sanitization would typically occur. `TopicEmbed.import` and `import_remote` create/update posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` using HTML content sourced from external RSS/remote pages (`SimpleRSS.parse open(...)` and `Readability::Document.new(open(url).read, ...)`) without any clear sanitization step. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, which will output that stored HTML verbatim. This is a concrete stored-XSS risk introduced by the diff if the external content contains script/event-handler payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `url` is interpolated directly into an HTML string without escaping in `topic_embed.rb:15`, causing stored XSS via URLs containing single quotes or angle brackets.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.import`, `url` is interpolated into an HTML snippet without escaping: `"#{url}"` and appended to `contents`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which still allows quotes or other dangerous characters in the remainder of the string (e.g., `http://example.com/' onmouseover='alert(1)`). Because imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html`, `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly (skipping Discourse’s normal cooking/sanitization pipeline), and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>`. This makes the unescaped URL injection a stored XSS vector.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `poll_feed.rb:31` uses `Kernel#open` with an admin-configurable URL, risking local file exposure via `file://` schemes if settings are compromised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `require 'open-uri'` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and then does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)`. `SiteSetting.feed_polling_url` is an admin-configurable string and there is no scheme/format validation (only `present?`). With `open-uri` loaded, `open(...)` will accept non-HTTP(S) URIs such as `file://...` and read local files, which could then be imported into posts via `TopicEmbed.import(...)`, enabling local file exposure if the setting is maliciously set (or an attacker gains the ability to set it).

adjudication_records.issue_text: `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` runs synchronously inside the `RetrieveTopic` job worker, blocking it; should be enqueued asynchronously via `Jobs.enqueue`.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a synchronous call to the scheduled job code: `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve` calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true. That can run inline (including network I/O via `open-uri`) during `RetrieveTopic` execution. However, this is not a clearly verifiable defect introduced by the diff: `RetrieveTopic` itself is already a background job (enqueued from `EmbedController`), so “blocking it” is not inherently incorrect, and the claim that it *should* be enqueued via `Jobs.enqueue` is an architectural preference rather than a demonstrable bug/security/correctness issue. The code appears intentionally written to try the feed immediately before falling back to HTTP fetch.

adjudication_records.issue_text: When no topic exists, a `RetrieveTopic` job is enqueued on every request, potentially flooding the job queue before Redis throttling takes effect.

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading`. There is no deduplication or throttling at enqueue time, so repeated requests for the same `embed_url` will enqueue a new `RetrieveTopic` job each time. The Redis throttle (`retrieved_recently?` using `$redis.setnx/expire`) exists only inside `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, which runs when the job executes, meaning the queue can still be flooded with redundant jobs that later no-op.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer-based host validation in `embed_controller.rb:26` can be bypassed using spoofed or empty referer headers.
`absolutize_urls` in `topic_embed.rb:58` checks port numbers regardless of scheme, causing incorrect absolute URL prefixes for `https://` on port 80 or `http://` on port 443.

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, the prefix is built as `"#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}"` and then the port is appended only if `uri.port != 80 && uri.port != 443`. This treats both 80 and 443 as “default” regardless of scheme. As a result, URLs like `https://example.com:80/...` or `http://example.com:443/...` will have their non-default ports incorrectly omitted from the generated absolute URLs (producing `https://example.com/...` or `http://example.com/...`, which point to different endpoints).
